Live capture becomes a worker pool: threads (default 1 = the historical sequential capture, cap 32, refused beyond rather than clamped). Claims CAS-issued from an atomic counter — claims are promises to send, attempts are settled sends; the sequential loop's attempt()<requested check was safe only because one goroutine ran it. Both pauses gate between sends in every worker (same placement as before, so a pause never splits a response). Miss-streak guard: per-worker streak, so a location that never matches stops in the same order of magnitude of requests the sequential guard produced (a global streak ÷ thread count would have cost threads×25 requests on a broken location). Cancellation classifies in the closer — several workers see ctx.Done at once and exactly one task.Stop lands, so the dashboard reads a cancelled capture as stopped. Wire: threads on the capture request; form gains the field with the shared-bound caveat in the hint. Tests: threads=1 never overlaps, threads=4 overlaps and collects every token, threads=33 refused, wide pool never claims one ordinal twice (origin stamps tokens at ACCEPT time — stamping at write time races across overlapping connections and mimics the duplicate-claim defect).
